page: Amazon Web Services im4gn.8xlarge is a storage-optimized server instance powered by the AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processor. This arm64 architecture features 32 dedicated physical cores running at 2.5 GHz, with no hyperthreading, resulting in 1.0 thread per core. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of RAM, providing a balanced 4.0 GB of memory per core. It is built on the AWS Nitro hypervisor and includes 15,000 GB of local NVMe SSD storage alongside a baseline network bandwidth of 50 Gbps.

Performance benchmarks indicate average multi-core capabilities, with a stress-ng multi-core CPU score of 48,576.94 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11,490.0. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, as demonstrated by a weak Geekbench single-core score of 941.0 and a poor single-threaded bzip3 decompression rate of 7.01 GB/sec. Memory performance is also mixed; while small-block cached read bandwidth is high at 1,893.97 GB/sec, the Passmark memory score is categorized as weak.

Given its massive 15,000 GB local NVMe SSD storage and solid database performance, such as 38.19 million operations per second in Redis SET benchmarks and average Passmark database operations, this instance is highly cost-efficient for storage-heavy and database workloads. The high local storage density relative to the ARM-based compute resources makes it suitable for large-scale databases, static web serving, and multi-threaded data processing, though it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or intensive LLM text generation.
